subject.title: [Feature]: Intelligent Model Fallback with Wildcard/Auto Selection

question: Which public provider-family fallback contract should OpenClaw support for text agent failover: wildcard/auto refs, grouped fallbackFamilies, catalog-derived fallbacks, or no new fallback surface?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the alternatives create different public config contracts, provider-routing semantics, and upgrade expectations that automation should not choose on its own.

options.title: Design one canonical fallback contract
options.body: Adopt one public contract and land it across schema, normalization, runtime fallback candidate construction, fallback availability checks, docs, and focused tests.

options.title: Narrow to catalog-derived fallbacks
options.body: Use the fallbacksFromModels direction from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/60922 and leave wildcard/auto and fallbackFamilies out of scope for now.

options.title: Keep explicit fallbacks only
options.body: Document explicit fallbacks and auth.order as the supported path, then close this feature direction as not planned.

recommendation.title: Design one canonical fallback contract
recommendation.body: Adopt one public contract and land it across schema, normalization, runtime fallback candidate construction, fallback availability checks, docs, and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is repeated work on the central model fallback resolver, docs, and config semantics around this exact surface.
